notes: Reference benchmark numbers for the score-card gauge. Two marks: stock Gemma 4 baseline (no harness) and harnessed average (full Duecare stack). The user's score is rendered relative to these so a 60% reads correctly as 'big lift over baseline, still room above'. Numbers are measured against a fixed eval set; when the eval set or rubric expands, re-run the eval and PR the new numbers here. Stakeholders re-running the headline measurement should set `eval_set_size`, `eval_run_date`, `git_sha`, and the rubric `version` they measured against — that becomes the audit trail.

stock.label: stock 6%
stock.title: Stock Gemma 4 baseline (no harness, no persona, no GREP/RAG/Tools/Online)
stock.notes: Average pct_score across the 207-prompt eval set with all harness layers OFF and the default Gemma 4 E4B-it persona-free.

harnessed.label: harnessed 88%
harnessed.title: Harnessed average (~88% on 207-prompt eval set)
harnessed.notes: Average pct_score across the 207-prompt eval set with persona + GREP + RAG + Tools all ON.

footnote: These reference numbers (stock 6%, harnessed 88%) were measured against v3.5 rubric (19 dims, eval set git_sha fcc7ab1). v3.6 (21 dims with two new harm-axis dims) is the current rubric used for live grading; the reference numbers will be re-measured against v3.6 before submission. Expected lift is similar or higher because the harm dims discriminate strongly between stock (which often ships operational tips) and harnessed (which refuses with grounding).
